CVE-2024-7598 concerns network policy enforcement for pods in a terminating namespace, which is behavior of the Kubernetes control plane and network plugins. The Azure Disk CSI driver imports only a few helper packages from the k8s.io/kubernetes module (pkg/apis/core, pkg/features, pkg/kubelet/server/metrics and the pkg/volume utility packages) and does not link any namespace or network policy code. See https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-7598

This CVE affects kube-apiserver, where the order in which objects are deleted during namespace termination is undefined (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126587). The Calico binaries embed k8s.io/kubernetes only as a Go module dependency, for API types, validation, and kube-proxy libraries. They do not include or run the kube-apiserver or namespace controller code paths, so the vulnerable code path is not reached.

The Calico binaries embed k8s.io/kubernetes only as a Go module dependency, for API types, validation, and kube-proxy libraries. They do not include the kubelet or gitRepo volume plugin packages, never run kubelet, and never mount gitRepo volumes, so the vulnerable code path is not reached.

CVE-2024-7598 is a NetworkPolicy bypass in Kubernetes. During namespace deletion the order in which objects are removed is not defined, so a network policy can be deleted before the pods it protects, leaving a window in which those pods run without policy enforcement. The flaw is in the Kubernetes control-plane namespace termination path. The Node Feature Discovery binaries shipped in this image do not run that control-plane code and do not contain the namespace controller. They link only Kubernetes API types and small helper packages, so the vulnerable path is not executed.

CVE-2025-1767 affects Kubernetes clusters that use the deprecated in-tree gitRepo volume plugin. The Node Feature Discovery binaries shipped in this image are not kubelet or kube-apiserver components and do not process pod volumes, so the vulnerable gitRepo volume execution path is not present in this image's runtime behavior.

CVE-2024-7598 concerns namespace deletion ordering, where pods could outlive their NetworkPolicies during namespace termination. The Kubernetes 1.33+ sources used for these kube-apiserver packages include OrderedNamespaceDeletion enabled by default, and the namespace deletion implementation deletes pods before other namespaced resources when that gate is enabled.

CVE-2024-7598 affects Kubernetes >=1.3.0 and has no fixed release in any Kubernetes line: every version carried in the DHI catalog, 1.34.12 through 1.37.1, reports it with no fix version. Selecting kubectl from a different source would therefore not clear this finding. Tracking upstream for a fix.

CVE-2024-7598 concerns namespace deletion ordering, where pods could outlive their NetworkPolicies during namespace termination. The upstream advisory names kube-apiserver as the affected component (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126587). The Kubernetes 1.33+ sources used for these kube-controller-manager packages include OrderedNamespaceDeletion enabled by default, and the namespace deletion implementation deletes pods before other namespaced resources when that gate is enabled. On 1.37 the feature gate is removed and pods are deleted first unconditionally.
